caption: I signed personal surety for a business that doesn't exist anymore. The loan doesn't know that. Anyone else still paying for something that already ended?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R22 400
p/m salary
Living in Oudtshoorn
slides.body:
Male, 37
Single, no kids
Job: Processing plant worker, ostrich abattoir (ran his own catering business until last year)
Net salary: R22 400 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: Downsized twice since the business closed. This is as small as I'm willing to go.

slides.title: Business debt repayment
slides.includes: R58 000 balance, 26% interest, 22 months left, taken out trying to keep the catering business afloat
slides.body: I signed personal surety for a business that doesn't exist anymore. The loan doesn't know that.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.body: I used to cook for forty people a weekend. Now I barely cook for myself.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: Needed for the shift start at the plant, no taxis run that early
slides.body: The one bill that hasn't changed since I closed the business.

slides.title: Takeaways & convenience
slides.includes: Garage food, the nights I can't face the stove
slides.body: I told myself I'd cook more once the business closed. I do less of it than when I was running a kitchen.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, insurance, phone & data, funeral policy, electricity, stokvel
slides.body: R7 500 that isn't the debt and isn't rent. It's the only part of this I can actually move.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R22 400. R4 200 of that goes to a business that closed fourteen months ago. At this pace it clears in 22.

slides.title: I stopped avoiding what the business still owes
slides.body:
I put the loan into Beyond Horizon's debt tracker the month the doors closed, just so I'd actually watch the balance move instead of ignoring the statement.

Twenty-two months left, and it finally feels like it's counting down instead of just sitting there.

No bank login needed.
